coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4
record.summary: Two 11-story office towers at 1655 & 1725 3rd St (combined ~584,000-586,200 sq ft, sources differ on the exact figure), LEED v4 Gold per Office Snapshots, developed by a joint venture of Alexandria Real Estate Equities (10%), Uber Technologies (45%) and the Golden State Warriors (45%), with SHoP Architects credited as architect by ArchDaily, completed in 2021 per SF Standard. Uber and the Warriors each lease office space at the property for their headquarters (The Real Deal, 2025); in 2023 Uber marketed all of 1725 3rd St for sublease and said that building was unoccupied (SF Standard).

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- each tower's footprint is an individually surveyed OpenStreetMap building outline (not a hand trace, not the shared Assessor parcel), cross-checked visually against Esri satellite imagery.
notes.digitized_from: Real OpenStreetMap building footprints for both towers (OSM ways 1410182008 '1655 3rd St / Uber Headquarters Building 3' and 1410183655 '1725 3rd St / Uber Headquarters Building 4'), unioned into one MultiPolygon.

facts.value: Joint venture (Event Center Office Partners) of the Golden State Warriors (45%), Uber Technologies (45%) and Alexandria Real Estate Equities (10%)

SHoP Architects, per ArchDaily's 'Uber Headquarters' project page (its listed area, 423,000 ft2, differs from these two towers' combined size); interiors of Buildings 3 and 4 by Huntsman Architectural Group (Office Snapshots)
~584,000 (Office Snapshots) to ~586,200 (The Real Deal, 2025) combined; 'more than 586,000' (CommercialCafe, 2020); sources disagree on the exact figure
LEED v4 Gold (also WELL), per Office Snapshots

Uber Technologies and the Golden State Warriors each lease office space at the property for their headquarters (The Real Deal, 2025). In May 2023 Uber marketed all of 1725 Third St for sublease and said that building was unoccupied; the marketing materials cite 73 parking spaces for that building; Uber's 2022 blog post (as quoted by SF Standard) said more than 3,500 employees would be based at its four-building headquarters.

milestones.text: Alexandria Real Estate's Q4 2017 earnings supplemental discloses a joint venture with Uber and the Golden State Warriors "expected to be formed in February 2018" for "two office buildings aggregating 580,000 RSF, adjacent to the Golden State Warriors arena, which are 100% leased to Uber," with Alexandria's $31.0 million initial equity contribution representing a 10% interest

Mortenson's Nov 2017 schedule has structural steel erection on the two office towers ending 8/18/2018; the project's 'topping out' is the completion of all structural steel, scheduled for 9/1/2018; no report of the actual completion found
Both towers complete construction (SF Standard: the four-building campus was initially completed during the pandemic in 2021; Office Snapshots lists a 2021 completion date)

changes.text: The record no longer says Uber has occupied both towers since January 2022 on a 20-year lease for about 4,000 employees, or that it leases the entire office component: The Real Deal (2025) says Uber and the Warriors each lease office space there, and SF Standard (2023) says Uber never occupied 1725 Third St and was marketing it for sublease. SHoP Architects is now cited to ArchDaily (with Huntsman credited for the interiors by Office Snapshots), the joint venture to The Real Deal, LEED v4 Gold to Office Snapshots, and completion to 2021 (SF Standard, Office Snapshots) instead of June 2021. The steel-erection dates are now labelled as Mortenson's November 2017 schedule rather than recorded events, and the Alexandria supplemental is dated January 2018, when it was filed. open_questions: On 2026-09-23 this record's map shape was moved off the Assessor parcel (block/lot 8722063; the record was renamed accordingly) because DataSF's own Assessor Parcel dataset gives this parcel and the neighboring Chase Center arena identical geometry (one shared master-condo superblock parcel). The shape is now the union of both towers' own real OpenStreetMap building footprints (OSM ways 1410182008 and 1410183655). How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).

Uber's SEC EDGAR company record lists 1725 3rd Street as its business address (read 2026-09-29), though a May 2023 SF Standard report said that specific building had never been occupied by Uber and was being marketed for sublease -- current occupancy is genuinely unclear and not resolved here.

DataSF business-registration data shows several Uber-internal registrations here (Bon Appetit @ Uber cafeteria service across multiple floors, Uber Freight Holding Corporation, a Mercedes-Benz-branded garage/showroom) not yet researched or added as facts.
No dedicated primary source (an Alexandria or Uber press release specifically) was found for the exact completion date of each tower individually; 2021 is used as a combined year.

No total development or construction cost for the two towers was found as of 2026-09-23. Press coverage only turns up financing and lease figures -- Uber's $136,000,000 payment for a 45% joint-venture stake, its $1,000,000,000 in lease payments over 20 years, and the $600,000,000 CMBS refinancing already cited above -- none of which is a stated construction or development cost, so none is recorded here.

Corrected 2026-09-29: the 'January 2022 occupancy', '20-year lease', '~4,000 employees' and '145 parking spaces' claims were removed because no source that could be read states them (Office Snapshots has no lease or headcount; SF Standard cites Uber's 2022 blog for 'more than 3,500 employees' across four buildings and says 1725 3rd St was never occupied). The ArchDaily page credits SHoP Architects but lists 423,000 ft2 and a 2022 year, so which buildings it covers is not confirmed. Completion is dated 2021 (SF Standard, Office Snapshots); no month is sourced.
